title: The integral proper projection formula
statement:
Work in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes and their $k$-morphisms. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside an algebraic closure, with ring of integers $\mathcal O_E$. Use its condensed coefficient ring and its pullbacks $\mathcal O_{E,T}=p_T^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], the ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], bounded constructible complexes $\Dbc$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and localizing closures with ambient small direct sums [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. All tensor products are the relative derived tensors of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], without completion. The projection formula map is the canonical adjoint transpose of the pullback tensor comparison followed by the tensor of the counit $p^*Rp_*K\to K$ with $p^*L$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact].

1. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the projection formula map
$$Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,Y}}L\longrightarrow Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}p^*L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.
2. For every standing scheme $T$, $\Loc(\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E))$ is closed under $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$. The same projection formula map is an isomorphism for $K\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ and $L\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text: A standing scheme T is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, hence the integral case of adicConstructibilityPredicateComparison identifies the adopted boundedConstructible predicate with constantModelBoundedConstructible. The ordinary derived tensor and the canonical moduleObjectProjectionMap are definitionally the adopted curried tensor and projectionMap component. No completion or new comparison morphism is introduced.

Compare the large-index intersection closure to the adopted Hom-universe localizing closure. Every existing coproduct has Hom-small nonzero support: its nonzero summands give distinct coordinate idempotents in the endomorphism set. Restrict the cofan to these indices, shrink them to the Hom universe, and use the coproduct universal property; omitted zero summands contribute unique maps. Thus every adopted localizing subcategory is closed under the existing larger coproducts. Minimality of the intersection gives the required containment. This is the same support argument as the recorded coproduct universe-extension lemma. Conversely, a localizing subcategory for the larger object universe is closed under Hom-small sums by lifting their index types and transporting along the discrete equivalence. This gives equality of the two closures.

Regard p as a morphism over Spec k and apply the bounded proper projection formula projection_bounded from the existing module-object implementation. Translate the bounded-constructibility hypotheses by step 1. The canonical right-adjoint projection map is definitionally moduleObjectProjectionMap.

For each standing scheme T prove tensor closure in the original large-index intersection, rather than inferring it from the containment of step 2. Tensor in either variable is exact and a left adjoint, so the inverse image of a localizing subcategory under it is localizing. The adopted bounded integral tensor theorem, transported by step 1, gives closure on generators. First fix a bounded second input and apply minimality in the first input; then fix an arbitrary first input in the closure and apply minimality in the second input. The existing localizingClosure_exists supplies the localizing property of the target closure. This proves the middle conjunct for every T, including zero inputs and existing empty coproducts.

Finite-type quasi-compact morphisms to the quasi-compact target have a uniform bound on fibre dimension. Field extension to the algebraic closure does not increase it. Apply integralProperDirectSums with that bound to obtain proper pushforward stability and preservation of ambient coproduct cofans. Step 2 identifies the two localizing predicates. Convert the cofan condition to preservation of discrete colimits, then apply the existing isIso_projectionMap_of_localizingBoundedConstructible. This is the two-variable determination proof: exactness and shift compatibility are supplied by the adopted ProjectionMapShift implementation; bounded pullback and tensor stability come from integralTensorInverseImage. The resulting map is definitionally the stated canonical mate.

proof_origin.place: Reuse the existing bounded proper formula and formal two-variable determination, supplying proper direct sums directly and explicitly comparing constructibility predicates and coproduct universes.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper.

1. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ the
   projection formula map
   $Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to Rp_*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*L)$ (underived
   completion, tensor over $\mathcal O_{E,Y}$) is an isomorphism in
   $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$.
2. The categories $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E))$ are closed under
   $\otimes^{\mathbf L}$, and the projection formula map is an isomorphism for
   $K\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ and $L\in\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text:
(1) By [sk-lem-int-tensor], $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}p^*L$ and
$Rp_*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}L$ are in $\Dbc$ (pullback and tensor product preserve
integral constructibility, and $Rp_*K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ by proper
finiteness, [sk-prop-int-compactness]); in particular both sides are derived
complete. Reduction modulo $\pi_E$ is exact, monoidal and commutes with $p^*$
and $Rp_*$, so it carries the map to the torsion projection formula map for
$K/\pi_E$ and $L/\pi_E$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathbf F_E)$, an isomorphism by
Stacks, Tag 0F0G. The cone $C$ of the map is derived complete with
$C\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathbf F_E=0$, hence $C=0$ by derived Nakayama
([sk-lem-pe-derived-nakayama]). This is the integral case of
[sk-thm-sfb-proper-base-change].

(2) *Tensor closure.* Fix $B\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$; the objects $A$ of
$\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ with $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B\in\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$
form a localizing subcategory ($-\otimes^{\mathbf L}B$ is exact and preserves
direct sums) which contains $\Dbc$ by [sk-lem-int-tensor],
hence everything; then fix $A$ and argue in $B$. *Extension.* $Rp_*$
preserves the localizing categories and direct sums there
([sk-prop-int-compactness]). Fix $L\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$: both sides are
exact, direct-sum preserving functors of $K$, isomorphic on $\Dbc$ by (1),
hence isomorphic on $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$ ([sk-lem-sf-determination]).
Then fix $K$ and argue in the same way in $L$.
